title: chore(store): update App Privacy and Data safety for telemetry
body:
**Priority:** P0
**Size:** S
**Ships with:** the 2.0.0 store build (#116)

Make both stores' declarations match the 2.0.0 binary, so no build that sends data ships under a "Data Not Collected" label. **Nothing here can be done before submission**: the answers and the privacy URL change together then (#116). The original 1.1.0 text is kept below.

### What leaves the device in 2.0.0

| Recipient | What | When |
|---|---|---|
| TelemetryDeck | the 5 events with their properties, including `language` and `languageSource` on launch; a SHA-256 hash of the install ID; a per-launch session ID; the IP address | only while "Share anonymous usage statistics" is on (it is on by default) |
| Expo (EAS Update) | OS, runtime and project; its own installation ID; the IP address; **after a failed start, the error message** (`Expo-Fatal-Error`, ≤ 1,024 chars) | every launch, whatever the switch says |
| Wikimedia Commons | photo thumbnails requested by URL; the IP address and the request details | rounds and the Study screen |

### Decided

- [x] The answers cover everything About states (#146, #155): the hashed install ID, the session code, the events with the app language, and the IP address.
- [x] **Crash data is declared** (owner, 2026-10-20). It covers the expo-updates error message sent after a failed start.
- [x] **"Anonymous" stays in the app text** (owner, 2026-10-20). The Data safety deletion answer describes the mechanism; see below.
- [x] **The privacy URL is versioned** (owner, 2026-10-19). `privacy.html` is the 1.x policy and `privacy/2/` the 2.0 policy, published by #157. A store's URL moves at the moment its 2.0 answers go in, because App Store Connect's privacy answers and policy URL belong to the app, not to a version.
- [x] **Wikimedia photo loading is not declared** (owner, 2026-10-20). Wikimedia is not a partner or an integrated SDK. The app fetches public files from its CDN, as a browser would, and neither the developer nor a partner can access what Wikimedia receives. About still tells users what Wikimedia receives (the IP address and the request details).

### At submission: Apple, App Store Connect → App Privacy (before Submit for Review)

- [ ] **Identifiers → Device ID**: not linked to the user, not used for tracking, purpose Analytics (TelemetryDeck's hashed install ID and session code).
- [ ] **Usage Data → Product Interaction**: not linked, not tracking, purpose Analytics (the events, including the app language).
- [ ] **Diagnostics → Crash Data**: not linked, not tracking, purpose App Functionality (the expo-updates error message).
- [ ] Re-confirm the EAS Update answer from the 1.0.0 correction (#61): the update check's installation ID, for App Functionality.
- [ ] **Privacy Policy URL** → `https://tovmassian.github.io/escuadra/privacy/2/`, in the same sitting.

### At submission: Google, Play Console → App content → Data safety (when the 2.0.0 AAB is uploaded)

- [ ] **App activity → App interactions**: collected, not shared, purpose Analytics.
- [ ] **Device or other IDs**: collected, not shared, purposes Analytics and App functionality.
- [ ] **App info and performance → Crash logs**: collected, not shared, purpose App functionality (the expo-updates error message).
- [ ] Encrypted in transit: yes.
- [ ] Deletion requests: none offered, because the statistics carry only a hashed random installation ID and cannot be traced to a person. Switching off "Share anonymous usage statistics" in About stops all sending. (A hashed ID plus an IP address is usually treated as pseudonymous under GDPR, so the answer describes the mechanism, not a legal status.)
- [ ] Keep it consistent with the EAS Update answer in the Android v1 listing.
- [ ] **Privacy policy URL** → `https://tovmassian.github.io/escuadra/privacy/2/`, in the same sitting.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both declarations match the telemetry allowlist and the `privacy/2/` policy
- [ ] Neither store claims "no data collected" for a build that sends telemetry

<details>
<summary>Original issue text (1.1.0)</summary>

**Priority:** P0  
**Size:** S

Update both stores' privacy declarations so they match the 1.1.0 binary. Submitting a build that collects data under a "Data Not Collected" label is the failure this prevents.

### Apple — App Store Connect → App Privacy

Per [TelemetryDeck's guidance](https://telemetrydeck.com/docs/articles/apple-app-privacy/):

- **Identifiers → Device ID** — not linked to the user, not used for tracking, purpose: Analytics
- **Usage Data → Product Interaction** — not linked, not tracking, purpose: Analytics
- Re-confirm how the EAS Update request is answered (decided during the 1.0.0 correction)

### Google — Play Console → App content → Data safety

- **App activity → App interactions** — collected, not shared, purpose: Analytics
- **Device or other IDs** — collected, not shared, purpose: Analytics
- Encrypted in transit: yes
- Whether users can request deletion — answer honestly given anonymised data and the in-app opt-out
- Keep consistent with the EAS Update answer from the Android v1 listing

### Timing

- Google: update when the 1.1.0 AAB is uploaded to any track
- Apple: update before sending 1.1.0 for review

### Acceptance criteria

- Both declarations match the telemetry allowlist and the published privacy policy
- Neither store is left claiming "no data collected" for a build that sends telemetry



</details>
why: The work happens in the store consoles, at submission of the 2.0.0 build: the skill asks.
